summary: The ACRC publishes yearly reward tables in its English annual reports: corruption rewards (cases, revenue recovered, amount paid) for every year from 2002 to 2024 and public-interest rewards from 2012 (first paid 2011) to 2024, plus monetary awards 2006-2011 and many cumulative totals. Later reports revise 2021-2023 (public-interest cases cut by more than half), so first-published and latest figures are both recorded. Korean press releases add 2019, 2020 and 2023 year totals, quarterly figures for 2024 to Q1 2026, and record cases. Reward rates and caps are traced through every version of the three enforcement decrees on law.go.kr, from 2-10% with a KRW 200 million cap (2002) to the flat 30% without a cap in force since 29 Sep 2026.

programs.name: ACRC rewards for corruption, public-interest and public-funds fraud reports (보상금)
programs.notes: Update to the existing row (launch date now confirmed). Corruption rewards began on 25 Jan 2002 under the Anti-Corruption Act (Act 6494) and its decree, run by the Korea Independent Commission Against Corruption and from 29 Feb 2008 by the ACRC under the ACRC Act. Public-interest rewards under the Public Interest Whistleblower Protection Act from 30 Sep 2011 (first paid in 2012 per the 2014 report, or Sep 2011 per the 2013 report); fraudulent-claims rewards under the Public Funds Recovery Act from 1 Jan 2020. A reward (보상금) is paid on application when a report directly recovers or increases public revenue or saves costs; a separate monetary award (포상금) can be paid without a recovery. Corruption reward schedule: 2-10% with a KRW 200 million cap (2002), 4-20% and 2 billion (30 Dec 2005), 4-30% and 3 billion (20 Oct 2015); public-interest: 4-20%, cap 1 billion (2011), 2 billion (2016), 3 billion (2018), 4-30% (19 Dec 2023), no cap (7 Aug 2024); public funds: flat 30%, cap 3 billion (2020), 4-30% (27 Sep 2024). From 29 Sep 2026 all three: flat 30% of the recovered amount, no cap (Presidential Decrees 36730-36732).
